instruction: I'd like to assess my current network quality. Please run a speed test on speedtest.net, then obtain the results from speedtest.net/results and record them in ~/Test/Speed/results.txt (if the folder doesn't exist, make it first). Structure the file with each metric on its own line, showing the metric name and value separated by a single space character.

metadata.explanation: Task involves executing a network quality assessment via speedtest.net, fetching the test results from speedtest.net/results, and persisting to a file. Evaluator validates that the file includes three key network indicators: Ping, Download, and Upload. This is a paraphrased version of the original task.

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete format verification: Evaluator only checks if the words 'Ping', 'Download', and 'Upload' appear anywhere in the file, but does not verify the required format

Missing structure validation: Instruction explicitly requires 'each metric on its own line, showing the metric name and value separated by a single space character', but file_contains metric does not verify this structure

Weak validation logic: The file_contains function (general.py:554-568) uses simple substring matching ('if text not in file_text'), which would pass incorrectly formatted files (e.g., 'Ping Download Upload' on one line, or these words appearing in prose)
No value validation: Does not verify that actual speed test VALUES are present alongside the metric names, only checks for keyword presence
Format requirement mismatch: A file containing the three keywords in any format/order would pass, even though the instruction specifies a precise format with line breaks and single-space separation
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Use check_list metric instead of file_contains to verify line-by-line structure with regex patterns
Add regex patterns to expected rules that match the format: '^Ping \d+', '^Download [\d.]+', '^Upload [\d.]+'
Consider using check_include_exclude with more specific patterns that enforce the 'metric_name value' format on separate lines
Alternative: Create a custom metric that parses each line and validates: (1) each metric is on its own line, (2) metric name and value are separated by exactly one space, (3) value is numeric
